In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the viscoelastic phase of PMII is a highly conducting ionic liquid.
the conductivity is a function of the temperature, the iodine concentration and the viscosity of the melt.
the conductivity of the polyiodides in the viscoelastic phase is a result of a combination of both ionic and Grotthuss conduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conductivity is not only a function of the ionic concentration, but also of the phase structure of the melt.
the conductivity of PMII melts is not only governed by the ionic liquid itself but also by the presence of polyiodides and their concentration.
we have demonstrated that the ionic liquid PMII is able to conduct electricity even in the solid state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ionic liquids are capable of conducting electricity at temperatures well below room temperature and that the conductivity of such melts is not only governed by the ionic concentration but also by the presence of a redox-active species.
a high conductivity of the ionic phase is possible at very low temperatures, even when the viscosity is very high.
a high ionic conductivity in the viscoelastic phase is possible, which could be of interest in applications such as electrochemical devices.
